title: Cadence Conductor weekplan and voice-ops notes (Mar 2027) - draft
body:
Context:
This is a working weekplan for the upcoming three-stage release (canary -> regional ramp -> full) for the Cadence Conductor feature set. Purpose: coordinate 'voice' handoffs (who speaks to customers/internal teams), clarify release-level checklists, and provide an annotated, day-by-day calendar for the release week.

High-level constraints / considerations:
- Target users: Hosted API customers and Dedicated tenants in NA region.
- Hard blackout window: 03/10 00:00–06:00 UTC for billing system maintenance — avoid large capacity shifts then.
- Telemetry gating: must see 24h stable tail latency on canary before regional ramp.
- Fallback model: route to model-v1.9-compat if conductor latency > 100ms p50.

Quick glossary:
- Conductor: orchestration layer changes (routing, step backoffs).
- Voice-ops: assigned people who will handle active comms (Slack, status page, customer pings).

Week-at-a-glance (annotated):
- Mon 2027-03-08: Preflight sync (09:00 PT) -> checklist walkthrough, validate smoke scripts, confirm canary pool size.
- Tue 2027-03-09: Dry-run canary in staging (13:00 PT) -> run synthetic traffic ramp, exercise rollback.
- Wed 2027-03-10: Small canary -> 02:00 PT rollout to 2 shards in NA-west (avoid billing blackout), 02:30 PT smoke + 4h observation window.
- Thu 2027-03-11: Canary review (09:00 PT) -> decision gate: proceed to regional ramp or rollback.
- Fri 2027-03-12: Regional ramp to NA-east + EU-west (gradual 10% -> 40% over 8h), close communication loop with SRE and CS.
- Sat 2027-03-13: Hold/recovery day.
- Sun 2027-03-14: Full rollout to remaining regions if telemetry green; otherwise extend ramp and schedule targeted fixes.

Voice-ops roster (primary / backup):
- Primary Incident Voice: Aisha Patel (on-call pager escalation)
- Customer comms & status: Priya Kapoor (prepare status page draft)
- Internal ops cadence lead: Jordan Chen (this doc owner)
- Rollback engineer: Luis Moreno
- Observability SME: Mateo Ruiz (tracing/metrics)

Release preflight checklist (must pass before canary):
- [ ] Build artifact signed and uploaded to artifact registry.
- [ ] Deploy manifests validated against schema-checker (CI job step 7).
- [ ] Smoke test suite pass (smoke:basic, smoke:kvcache, smoke:latency).
- [ ] Canary pool sizing confirmed and quota reservations in place.
- [ ] Runbook stub (this doc) shared to #deployments and pinned.
- [ ] Customer-facing post prepared (Priya) and pre-approved by legal for wording.

Canary execution checklist (during rollout):
- Start window set to low traffic period for affected regions.
- Incremental traffic ramp plan: 1% -> 5% in first 30m -> 15% in 2h -> monitor.
- Immediate health gates: error-rate < 0.5%, p95 latency delta < 20% from baseline.
- Manual holdpoints at 15m, 2h, and 6h marks.
- Fast rollback trigger: sustained error-rate > 1% for >10m or latency p95 >50% baseline for 15m.

Telemetry & dashboards to watch (primary signals):
- Request success ratio (per model, per region)
- p50/p95/p99 latency by endpoint
- QPS and CPU/GPU utilization per shard
- Model-specific token generation time and KV-cache hit rates
- Alert: "conductor-backpressure" if queue length > 200 for 5m
- Sampling traces for anomalous requests (capture full prompt + token timing for 1% of traffic)

Annotated day-level notes (operational hints / known riskiest pieces):
- Mon prep: bring a minimal set of smoke prompts that exercise long-context behavior — past deployments missed this and regressed.
- Dry-run staging: intentionally bump sequence lengths to 1.5x typical to force slow-paths in runtime.
- Canary: watch for subtle regression in reranking route (we changed tokenization for short prompts).
- Regional ramp: prefer expanding to regions with lower tail-latency first to reduce noise.

Draft release notes (customer-facing - short form):
- Title: Cadence Conductor: smarter request routing and reduced cold-starts
- Summary: This release improves routing heuristics for multi-tenant workloads and reduces first-request latency for pinned model variants. Customers may see better throughput and slightly reduced per-token cost for bursty workloads.
- Notable changes:
  - Optimized routing policy that favors locality and cache-warmth.
  - Improved KV-cache priming logic that reduces cold-starts for pinned models.
  - Small tokenization tweak for short prompts (may affect length-sensitive reranking).
- Impact & mitigations: If you observe changes in reranking behavior, please open support ticket linking a short transcript; we have a regression monitor and can pin previous behavior per-tenant.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Can we extend automatic prefix cache prewarm to Dedicated tenants without quota hits? (action: @Luis to validate with infra by Tue).
- Do we need a separate customer opt-out for the tokenization tweak? Legal asked for a short clause. (action: @Priya to draft).
- Should telemetry sampling for traces be temporarily raised to 5% during the canary? Observability cost impact unknown.

Post-release followups (30-day checklist):
- Week 0: daily pulse report for 7 days (Jordan sends summary to #deployments each morning).
- Week 1: run A/B evaluation on reranking prompts and publish short summary to product team.
- Week 2–4: monitor quality regressions; if model-specific drift detected, schedule rollback or soft-fix.
- 30 days: retrospective meeting with SRE/Product/CS to decide if rollout pattern should be generalized.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep rollout windows short and explicit in calendar invites to avoid accidental timezone confusion.
- Encourage SRE to run local-scale reproducer for any p95 spikes before escalating.
- Save canary snapshots (traces + sample prompts) in /artifacts/cadence-conductor/canary-2027-03 for postmortem.

Links and references:
- JIRA: JIRA-RI-4321 (conductor routing + cache work)
- Confluence baseline: confluence:release-cadence-templates
- Slack channel: #deployments (pinned checklist and preflight notes)

If anything changes, update this doc immediately and call a preflight recheck.
